correctness.rationale: For n>=2, H_n=K_{n,n} square K2 with arbitrary independent proper n-color horizontal factorizations on the two layers and one shared vertical color has 4n vertices and n+1 perfect-matching color classes M_c, each 2n edges. Connectivity of W union M_c forces |W|-|W cap M_c|>=2n-1. Sum across partitioning color classes yields n|W|>=(n+1)(2n-1), so |W|>=2n+1. Construct W as n-1 horizontal edges at a0 in layer0, n horizontal edges at b0 in layer1, plus vertical edges at a0 and b0. It has 2n+1 edges. Contracting vertical color gives a spanning double-star; for any horizontal perfect matching, layer1 is connected, layer0 has at most an isolated matched pair at b0 plus its main component, and the selected vertical edges connect both to layer1. Thus the formula holds uniformly for every permitted independent pair of factorizations, not only matched identical colorings.

evidence: Dawkins et al product statements as inspected require bipartite factors both with parts of size >=2; K2 fails this hypothesis.
General component lower bound gives only the lower 2n+1.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The present robust construction supplies the matching upper bound for the excluded prism and independent factorization choice; any stronger general coverage in unread text remains a risk.

evidence: General bound n|W|>=(n+1)(2n-1) does not construct any W meeting it.
Layer-one star, partial layer-zero star, two vertical bridges work simultaneously for arbitrary independent matchings.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The explicit factorization-independent upper construction is an additional implication absent from the inspected prior general component theorem.

evidence: Color-connecting set W means W union M_c is connected for every monochromatic perfect matching.
In H_n these monochromatic matchings partition the full proper colored graph.

value.rationale: The color-connecting wild number is a natural graph invariant and the general component obstruction alone leaves the upper bound open. The robust double-star construction supplies a sharp exact infinite-family formula even when horizontal one-factorizations differ across layers, a concrete extension outside known product hypotheses.

limitations: Only the stipulated minimum colorings with one uniform vertical color and horizontal common palette are covered; other proper minimum colorings may behave differently.
No classification of all minimum wild sets and no unbalanced K_{m,n} prism formula.
